question: This question asks about the preceding passage as a whole. Suppose the writer's primary purpose had been to persuade readers that commuters should put away their phones while they wait for trains. Would this essay accomplish that purpose?

options.A: Yes, because the narrator first notices the birds only on the morning the phone dies, which presents the phone as the one thing in the way.
options.B: No, because the essay is chiefly about Corinne's morning count of the birds and the method she uses to keep it.
options.C: Yes, because it presents Corinne, standing still with her head tilted toward the trees, as the commuter whose habit the narrator comes to copy.
options.D: No, because the narrator still reads email every morning, only on the train instead of the platform, and never urges anyone to change.

options.A: Electronics makers often release a new version of a laptop every year or so, sometimes in the fall.

This question asks about the preceding passage as a whole. Suppose the writer's primary purpose had been to explain the scientific method FitzRoy used to turn weather reports into forecasts. Would this essay accomplish that purpose?

options.A: No, because it is concerned chiefly with the scientists who attacked the forecasts in the 1860s rather than with FitzRoy and his work.
options.B: Yes, because it explains that FitzRoy called his notices informed judgments, a description of how they were reasoned out.
options.C: No, because it tells how the forecasts began, drew criticism, and were stopped, but not how FitzRoy turned reports into predictions.
options.D: Yes, because it describes how reports of wind and air pressure from distant ports were gathered in a single office by telegraph.
